cards.explanation: The answer is the Jordan. Joshua and all the Israelites leave Shittim and go as far as the Jordan, where they camp before crossing over (Joshua 3:1). Notice the "…before crossing over." part, friends. Nobody is moving in yet, they're just parking at the edge of a very big river.

The answer is to set out from their spots and follow it. The officers tell the people, "When you see the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God being carried by the Levitical priests, you are to set out from your positions and follow it." (Joshua 3:3). The signal is simple, friends. See the ark moving, then you move.

The answer is so they can see the way to go. The officers say to keep that distance "…so that you can see the way to go, since you have never traveled this way before." (Joshua 3:4). Think of trying to read a map with someone's shoulder in your face. Space helps you see.

The reason is that tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among them. Joshua says, "Consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you." (Joshua 3:5). The reason points straight at what the LORD is about to do, friends. I'd have cleaned my whole apron for that news.

The answer is Moses. The LORD says He will exalt Joshua so all Israel may know He is with him "…just as I was with Moses." (Joshua 3:7). That's a big thing to hear when you're the one stepping up. I bet Joshua felt every bit of it.

The answer is False. The LORD tells Joshua to command the priests, "When you reach the edge of the waters, stand in the Jordan." (Joshua 3:8). No staying on the bank with dry toes, friends. They go in.
The answer is False. Joshua says to choose twelve men from the tribes of Israel, "…one from each tribe." (Joshua 3:12). So it's one man per tribe, friends, not a whole dozen from Levi.

The answer is that the water will stop and stand up in a heap. Joshua says that when the priests' feet touch down in the Jordan, "…its flowing waters will be cut off and will stand up in a heap." (Joshua 3:13). Water standing up in a heap, friends. If somebody told me that before breakfast, I'd ask them to say it again, slower.

The answer is False. Joshua 3:15 says the Jordan overflows its banks throughout the harvest season. That's high water, friends, not low. I think that makes the walk to the water's edge a serious step.
The answer is True. Once the water is cut off, "…the people crossed over opposite Jericho." (Joshua 3:16). The river stops and the people cross right across from the city of Jericho, friends.

The answers are dry and nation. The priests carrying the ark "…stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan…" (Joshua 3:17). Dry ground in the middle of a river, friends. I'd tell that story at every party. The priests stood firm while all Israel crossed over "…until the entire nation had crossed the Jordan." (Joshua 3:17). Every last person made it across, and the priests held their spot the whole time.
